item.title: Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng meets with Apple Executive Chairman Tim Cook
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
BEIJING, Oct. 12 -- Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, met with Tim Cook, executive chairman of the board of directors of Apple Inc., at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on Monday. During their meeting, He said implementing the common understandings between the two heads of state and building a constructive relationship of strategic stability on the basis of respect, fairness and reciprocity are conducive to the stability and development of the economies of both countries and the world, and will provide stable expectations and a sound business environment for multinational companies. China welcomes science and technology companies from all countries, including Apple, to continue deepening mutually beneficial and win-win cooperation with China and to share the opportunities of Chinese modernization, He said. Cook said Apple is fully confident in its long-term development in China and will serve as a bridge of communication within the business community, contributing more to promoting the stable and sound development of U.S.-China economic and trade relations.

item.title: China ready to expand cooperation with New Zealand in services trade, new energy sectors, says premier
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
BEIJING, Oct. 12 -- China is ready to work with New Zealand to tap the potential of trade in services and expand cooperation in sectors such as new energy vehicles, photovoltaics and wind power, Chinese Premier Li Qiang said Monday during a phone conversation with New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon. China-New Zealand relations have maintained steady and sound momentum, with new progress made in cooperation across various fields, Li said. Meanwhile, the international situation remains complex and evolving, with unilateralism and protectionism continuing to weigh on the global economy, he said, adding that calls from the international community to safeguard the multilateral system and strengthen openness and cooperation are growing louder. As supporters and practitioners of multilateralism and free trade, China and New Zealand should strengthen communication and coordination, Li said. Noting that the two countries will mark the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations next year, Li said China stands ready to work with New Zealand to carry forward their traditional friendship, expand mutually beneficial cooperation and deepen their comprehensive strategic partnership, injecting fresh impetus into the stability, development and prosperity in both countries, the region and the world. Li said China is willing to work with New Zealand to remain partners that respect each other and pursue mutual benefit and win-win cooperation. He called on both sides to continue to expand the scale and improve the quality of bilateral trade in goods, tap the potential of trade in services, and expand cooperation in areas such as new energy vehicles, photovoltaics and wind power to deliver more tangible results. The premier expressed hope that the two sides will accelerate negotiations on a negative list for trade in services under the China-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement and achieve substantive progress at an early date. The two countries should facilitate people-to-people exchanges and deepen exchanges and cooperation in culture, tourism, education, young people and sub-national entities to strengthen the foundation of friendship between their peoples, Li said. As members of the Asia-Pacific family, China and New Zealand should also strengthen cooperation within the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) framework and actively advance the building of an Asia-Pacific community, he added. For his part, Luxon said New Zealand-China relations are developing steadily, with practical cooperation advancing across various fields and benefiting the peoples of both countries. New Zealand attaches great importance to its relationship with China and remains firmly committed to the one-China policy, he said. New Zealand is willing to take the opportunity of next year's 55th anniversary of diplomatic relations to strengthen high-level exchanges with China, deepen mutual understanding and trust, and enhance practical cooperation in trade, tourism, new energy and other areas to advance the comprehensive strategic partnership, he said. Luxon also expressed New Zealand's support for China's hosting of the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting. The two sides also exchanged views on international and regional issues of common concern.

item.title: Xi congratulates Madise on assuming Estonian presidency
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
BEIJING, Oct. 12 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Monday extended congratulations to Ulle Madise on her assumption of office as president of Estonia. Xi said that China and Estonia enjoy a traditional friendship and that bilateral relations have maintained steady development in recent years, with continued progress in exchanges and cooperation across various fields, bringing benefits to the two peoples. Xi said that he attaches great importance to the development of China-Estonia relations and stands ready to work with President Madise to take the 35th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries this year as an opportunity to enhance political mutual trust, expand mutually beneficial cooperation, deepen people-to-people and cultural exchanges, and continuously enrich the contemporary connotations of bilateral relations.

item.title: Xi, Papua New Guinea's governor-general exchange congratulations over 50th anniversary of diplomatic ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
BEIJING, Oct. 12 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and Bob Dadae, governor-general of Papua New Guinea, on Monday exchanged congratulations on the 50th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries. In his message, Xi noted that Papua New Guinea is a good friend, good partner and good brother of China in the Pacific island region. Over the past 50 years since the establishment of diplomatic ties, the two countries have deepened political mutual trust, achieved fruitful results in mutually beneficial cooperation, and expanded people-to-people exchanges, raising bilateral relations to new heights, Xi said. These achievements have benefited the two peoples and injected strong impetus into building a China-Pacific Island countries community with a shared future, said Xi. Noting that he attaches great importance to the development of China-Papua New Guinea relations, Xi said that he stands ready to work with Dadae to take the 50th anniversary of diplomatic relations as an opportunity to carry forward traditional friendship, strengthen exchanges and cooperation across various fields, and elevate the comprehensive strategic partnership between China and Papua New Guinea to a new level, so as to deliver greater benefits to the two peoples. For his part, Dadae said that over the past 50 years, bilateral relations have made significant progress, benefiting both countries and their peoples. Papua New Guinea cherishes the longstanding friendship with China, firmly upholds the one-China principle, and looks forward to taking the 50th anniversary of diplomatic relations as an opportunity to further deepen and advance bilateral relations, he said. On the same day, Chinese Premier Li Qiang also exchanged congratulations with Papua New Guinea's Prime Minister James Marape. China is willing to work with Papua New Guinea to take the 50th anniversary of diplomatic relations as an opportunity to promote high-quality Belt and Road cooperation and advance the comprehensive strategic partnership between China and Papua New Guinea, Li said in the message. For his part, Marape said that the Papua New Guinean government highly appreciates China's significant contributions to the country's economic and social development. Papua New Guinea will continue to uphold the one-China principle it has long adhered to, deepen mutually beneficial cooperation with China across various fields and advance the development of the comprehensive strategic partnership between the two countries, said Marape.

item.title: Chinese vice premier urges strengthening of advanced manufacturing
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
CHANGCHUN, Oct. 10 -- Chinese Vice Premier Zhang Guoqing has called for strengthening and expanding advanced manufacturing, enhancing the self-reliance and controllability of industrial chains, and accelerating the building of a modern industrial system with advanced manufacturing as its backbone. Zhang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks during his inspection tour in the northeastern province of Jilin from Thursday to Saturday. He stressed the need to make greater efforts to promote the deep integration of scientific and technological innovation with industrial innovation, encourage enterprises, especially large ones, to strengthen basic research, and achieve breakthroughs in a number of key core technologies and generic technologies. Efforts should be made to develop next-generation intelligent manufacturing, accelerate the widespread application of digital, intelligent and green technologies, and promote the renewal and upgrading of traditional industries, Zhang said. He also emphasized the need to strengthen basic theoretical studies on scientific research instruments and give full play to the role of key scientific and technological research forces, including national laboratories, national research institutions, high-level research universities and leading sci-tech enterprises. Zhang urged efforts to enhance common supporting capabilities for scientific research instruments, such as system integration, standards and metrology, pilot-scale verification, and inspection and testing, so as to promote the application and dissemination of independently developed technologies and products.

item.title: Chinese state councilor urges athletes to step up preparations for 2028 Olympics
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09
BEIJING, Oct. 9 -- Chinese State Councilor Shen Yiqin urged Chinese athletes to build on their experiences from the 20th Asian Games and continue working hard in preparation for the 2028 Olympic Games. Shen made the remarks on Friday in Beijing during a meeting with the Chinese delegation to the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, which concluded on Sunday. China topped the medal table for the 12th consecutive edition, collecting 169 gold, 89 silver and 83 bronze medals to achieve its best medal haul at an overseas Asian Games. Shen extended her congratulations to the delegation for its brilliant performances, saying the athletes had brought glory to the country and its people through their patriotism, determination, teamwork, confidence and sportsmanship. With less than two years remaining before the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games, Shen urged athletes to address their shortcomings and weaknesses, maintain their preparations and further strengthen China's position as a leading Olympic sporting nation.

item.title: Xi calls for firm confidence, solid steps for China's national rejuvenation
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-30
BEIJING, Sept. 30 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday called on the nation to forge ahead with firm confidence and take solid steps to achieve the great national rejuvenation. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks at a reception held at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China. China's National Day falls on Oct. 1. Li Qiang presided over the reception. Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang, Li Xi and Han Zheng attended the event along with around 800 guests. "The great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation is unstoppable," Xi said. "As long as we remain confident, stay focused on our goals and move forward steadily, step by step, success will ultimately belong to the great CPC, the great Chinese people and the great People's Republic of China." He noted that over the past 77 years, the Party has led the Chinese people in achieving two miracles: rapid economic growth and enduring social stability. "We take immense pride in the extraordinary achievements of New China and have full confidence in the bright prospects of Chinese modernization," he said. Since the beginning of this year, the Chinese economy has continued to progress despite mounting pressure and achieved innovation-driven and high-quality development, demonstrating strong resilience and vitality, he said. Efforts should be made to sustain this momentum, promote innovation-driven, high-quality and sound economic development, take practical steps to safeguard and improve people's livelihoods, and meet the targets and tasks set for the year, so as to ensure a good start to the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030), he said. Xi stressed the need to remain firmly committed to the policy of "one country, two systems," under which the people of Hong Kong administer Hong Kong, the people of Macao administer Macao, and both regions enjoy a high degree of autonomy. He went on to say that the central government will support Hong Kong and Macao in integrating more fully into the country's overall development. The central government is committed to maintaining their long-term prosperity and stability, Xi added. He also called for efforts to deepen exchanges and cooperation across the Taiwan Strait, resolutely fight secessionist forces seeking "Taiwan independence," oppose external interference, and promote the peaceful development of cross-Strait relations to advance national reunification. China will stick to its independent foreign policy of peace, advance the implementation of the four major global initiatives it proposed, and promote the building of a community with a shared future for humanity to contribute greater certainty and positive energy to a turbulent world, Xi said.

item.title: China issues revised regulations on implementation of audit law
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-24
BEIJING, Sept. 24 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang has signed a State Council decree promulgating revised regulations on the implementation of the audit law. The revised regulations, which consist of 7 chapters and 64 articles, will take effect on Dec. 1. Highlighting the need to refine and improve audit supervision, the regulations specify the scope and content of audits over fiscal revenues and expenditures, and bring the management and use of state-owned resources into the scope of special audit investigations, among others. To ensure that audit work is free from interference, the regulations add provisions on a registration and reporting system for any unwarranted attempts to inquire about or interfere with audit matters. All departments of the State Council and local authorities at all levels shall strengthen overall coordination, oversee rectification of problems uncovered in audits, and establish and improve relevant systems.

item.title: China tightens accountability for officials regarding ecological, environmental damage
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
BEIJING, Aug. 25 -- Chinese officials found responsible for serious ecological and environmental damage will be held accountable for life, even if they have since left their posts, according to a recently released policy document. Issued by the General Office of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and the General Office of the State Council, the document outlines the cases that can lead to official accountability, as well as the disciplinary measures that may follow. The accountability framework was originally released in 2015. An official with the Organization Department of the CPC Central Committee said an update was necessary as China has entered a stage of high-quality development featuring accelerated green and low-carbon growth, while the CPC Central Committee has issued a series of new requirements on ecological and environmental protection in recent years. The revised rules broaden the scope of accountability beyond leading Party and government officials to include senior officials at public institutions, development zones and state-owned enterprises. China has pledged to bring carbon dioxide emissions to a peak before 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality before 2060. The revised document specifies that local officials who fail to effectively advance these efforts will also be held accountable. Meanwhile, the official from the Organization Department of the CPC Central Committee noted that accountability for ecological and environmental damage must be precise and evidence-based. "It should neither dampen officials' enthusiasm for work, nor undermine the credibility of the Party and the government." China has stepped up ecological and environmental protection efforts. During the second round of the central ecological and environmental protection inspections, conducted from May 2020 to June 2022, a total of 3,371 people were held accountable. The third round of such inspections is currently underway. The revised accountability rules also bring them into line with China's Ecological and Environmental Code, which officially took effect on Aug. 15.
